title: Offcut — a shared cutting-stock workbench
tagline: Measure and protect your stock. Let your browser agent compare cutting plans. Review before releasing a cut sheet.
artifact_status: Complete current1.1.0 source/app behavior, native/model workflow and actual165-second English-audio/40-cue demo verified. Source/runtime, final edited-media and versioned-release/download observations have separate records. Entrant attestations, actual Public YouTube playback and actual Devpost Submitted remain user-owned steps.

working_name.name: Offcut
working_name.meaning: An offcut is a piece left after cutting a longer length of material.
working_name.naming_status: This is the working name used by the deployed app, not an attestation that the entrant selected or approved the submission title.

description_sections.question: Why your use case is a strong fit for WebMCP
description_sections.heading: Measured stock is a structured problem
description_sections.text: Offcut is for small workshops, makerspaces and individual makers arranging straight crosscuts from boards and existing offcuts of the same material and cross-section. A maker records usable lengths and exact part quantities, sets blade kerf, and protects stock needed elsewhere. In a chat-only workflow, that state has to be copied out and the answer reconciled with the workbench. WebMCP gives the browser agent structured access to the same committed measurements and revision the maker sees. The agent requests checked alternatives; Offcut's deterministic solver, not the language model or a screenshot estimate, checks quantities and physical material balance.

description_sections.question: How it creates a better user experience
description_sections.heading: Show the trade-off instead of hiding it in a waste score
description_sections.text:
People edit stock and part lists, protect individual lengths, and compare proportional layouts under three objectives. Sawdust, short scrap, reusable remnants and unopened stock remain distinct; full-reference disclosures identify the actual plans, boards and requirements.

The verified 1.1.0 illustrative job produces 14 parts totalling 7,000 mm with A-01 protected, 3 mm kerf and a 400 mm reusable threshold. Use less stock and Handle fewer boards each open 7,200 mm across three pieces: 42 mm sawdust, 158 mm short scrap and no reusable remnant. Keep useful offcuts opens 10,080 mm across six pieces: 42 mm sawdust, no short scrap and 3,038 mm reusable remnants. Avoiding 158 mm of short scrap therefore opens 2,880 mm more stock and handles three more pieces. These are computed sample results, not measured real-workshop, time, money or carbon savings; later use of the remnants is not demonstrated.

description_sections.question: Describe what people and agents can do together that was difficult or impossible before
description_sections.heading: One shared workshop, from comparison to re-review
description_sections.text:
Before: a maker copying a stock list into chat has to reconcile advice with the current workshop and translate it back into a cut sheet. With Offcut: the person measures and protects stock; the agent reads that committed revision, requests alternatives, compares their explicit constraints and stages one exact complete proposal. The person checks its identities, quantities, offsets and kerf, then separately acknowledges and approves that ID. The agent can export only the exact approved fresh plan, not whichever draft happens to be selected.

If the person commits a kerf change from 3 to 4 mm, the old plan becomes stale and its approval is invalidated. The agent must read the new revision, replan and stop for a new review. Unfinished text is different: PENDING_MEASUREMENTS holds review requests until edits are finished or cancelled, without silently saving text or revoking approval per keystroke. The shared page carries the proposal-to-decision handoff and the reason an earlier decision is no longer valid; it does not reserve or consume stock.

description_sections.question: Briefly explain how you implemented WebMCP
description_sections.heading: Native tools backed by the same checked domain operations
description_sections.text: Offcut is a static React/TypeScript application built with Vite. It registers six JSON-schema-defined JavaScript tools in the top-level page through real document.modelContext, with only the real native navigator.modelContext Chrome-149 compatibility path: get_workshop, plan_cuts, inspect_plan, compare_plans, stage_plan_for_review and export_cut_list. UI and tools share the workshop store and deterministic branch-and-bound planner. Planning and staging require the current expectedRevision; pending edits hold staging/approval, and incomplete, stale or unapproved plans cannot be released. Approval, stock unlocking and measurement mutation are absent from the registered tools. Registration readiness is not a model connection. There is no polyfill, application backend, embedded model or website API key; manual planning works without WebMCP. The model uses integer-millimetre one-dimensional crosscuts and one kerf per produced part. Search is capped at 100,000 nodes, with optimality reported only when proved. It is a planning estimate, not machine control or a safe-cutting guarantee.

demonstration_disclosure: The current1.1.0 demonstration uses25 actual stateless model decisions, including19 Chrome-native tool calls and6 local finish decisions, through an external recording harness. The edited165-second English-audio/40-cue video shows actual live app pixels with clearly identified retained native/UI evidence summaries. Stock protection, navigation, acknowledgement/button approval, CSV download and measurement edits are separate browser UI automation. Not a ChatGPT interface recording, physical-human-presence proof, latency benchmark, Public YouTube publication, Submitted entry or jury outcome.

novelty_and_precedents.boundary: Cutting-stock optimization is established work. OpenCutList already supports standard/offcut boards, blade thickness, trimming and cutting diagrams. Offcut's contribution is the shared committed workshop, explicit agent comparison, exact review/release and revision invalidation in one browser page, not a claim to invent cutting optimization or to be the first such product worldwide.
novelty_and_precedents.reuse_boundary: This is a workflow precedent, not code or artwork copied into Offcut. No measured customer, workshop, time, money or carbon impact is claimed.

demonstrated_case.name: The little library — original illustrative measurements
demonstrated_case.data_origin: Original sample inputs included with Offcut; listed results were actually executed on the current1.1.0 workbench. No real customer or workshop-impact study is represented.
demonstrated_case.important_setup_detail: Loading the sample does not protect A-01 automatically. Protect that 3,000 mm length in the UI before solving to reproduce these results.
demonstrated_case.interpretation: All three plans produce the same 7,000 mm of finished parts and leave A-01 untouched. Relative to least_stock, least_waste has 158 mm less short scrap, 2,880 mm more opened stock, three more stock pieces handled and 3,038 mm more reusable remnants; sawdust remains 42 mm. Reusable remnants are not discarded waste, but their later use is not demonstrated.

testing_instructions.application_access: Open the live URL directly. Offcut requires no application account, login credentials, payment, API key, installation or local server for judging.
testing_instructions.safe_test_context: Use a fresh private browser window or test profile so sample replacement does not overwrite your own saved measurements. Keep the same workbench document open during planning, review and export; plans and approvals are page-session state. No physical cutting is needed for judging.
common_setup: Open https://ilyanaxo.github.io/offcut-webmcp/. Use Load illustrative sample, then Replace with sample in the confirmation dialog, to establish the inputs listed in demonstrated_case.

Protect A-01, the 3,000 mm Long board, using Available — protect stock Long board (A-01). After activation its name is Protected — unprotect stock Long board (A-01), with pressed state true. Leave all other stock available and do not add tool-side exclusions. Check the 3 mm kerf, 400 mm reusable threshold and four requirement rows listed above.

Commit field edits with Enter or by leaving the field; Escape cancels an unfinished field edit. Complete or cancel new rows too. The shared pendingMeasurements flag remains true until all unfinished edits are resolved. Human solving/review/approval/CSV/print are held; native planning reads committed measurements, while an otherwise valid native review request rejects with PENDING_MEASUREMENTS before any dialog, blur or save.
manual_no_login_path: Choose Use less stock and click Find a cutting plan. Repeat for Handle fewer boards and Keep useful offcuts. Compare the retained proposals with demonstrated_case.results, including quantities, sawdust, short scrap and useful remnants. Open Full comparison references & restrictions to inspect IDs and canonical additional/effective restriction sets. With A-01 protected and no additional exclusions, the fresh complete alternatives have the same effective constraints and never use A-01.

Select the least-stock proposal and click Review this plan after finishing/cancelling edits. Open Full plan, board & part IDs using Tab then Enter/Space, or touch, to check the raw stored plan, board and requirement IDs. Check quantities, numerical offsets and physical settings against the sample. Approve cut sheet is disabled before acknowledgement. A different staged ID resets acknowledgement and focuses the review heading; the same-ID no-op does not reset or jump.

As the human reviewer, tick the checkbox labelled I checked the usable lengths, kerf and part quantities against my measurements. Then click Approve cut sheet. These are separate UI actions, not tool calls or physical human-presence authentication.

Click Download approved CSV. Its filename is offcut-${slug}-r${revision}-${plan.id}.csv, with the full actual generated plan ID; there are 17 columns, with Part ID (cut.requirementId) at zero-based index 8 before Part. The canonical guide gives the complete column order. Duplicate part labels remain distinguishable by IDs. Print approved cut sheet opens browser printing; Save as PDF is a browser option, not an Offcut tool. CSV/print use all produced-part rows and release a planning document, not a fabrication or inventory transaction.

Select a different retained draft after approval, or repeat the approved request to obtain a reused solution with a new unapproved record ID. The release panel still identifies the old exact approved plan separately; download/print use it, not the selected or reused draft. Pending edits pause human release without discarding that saved approval; a real committed change invalidates it.

native_browser_setup.supported_entry_paths: The challenge permits ChatGPT's desktop built-in browser or Google Chrome 149 or later with WebMCP enabled. Follow the dated host prerequisites below; Offcut itself does not supply or connect a model.
native_browser_setup.chrome_flag_instruction: Enable the flag and restart Chrome before opening the live app, as the official Chrome guide and challenge rules describe. For an isolated test-browser launch, the native feature flag is --enable-features=WebMCP.
native_browser_setup.browser_agent_host_distinction: The Chrome flag exposes the native browser API; it does not create an agent. A configured agent host must discover and invoke the site's tools. That host may have its own account or provider requirements, separate from Offcut's no-login website.
native_browser_setup.native_surface: Offcut prefers real document.modelContext on the modern native surface and uses only the real native navigator.modelContext compatibility surface in Chrome 149. It does not install a polyfill.
native_browser_setup.readiness_check: Look for Native WebMCP ready and six registered tools in the Browser agent area. This confirms actual native registration, not that ChatGPT or another particular model has connected. Human UI actions and native tool invocations are attributed separately in activity.
native_browser_setup.ordinary_browser_fallback: If the browser reports native WebMCP unavailable, use the complete manual path above. Do not treat manual actions or simulated tool calls as a verified model demonstration.
chatgpt_prerequisites: Update to the latest ChatGPT desktop app and use its built-in browser with ChatGPT Work or Codex.
Select GPT-5.6 Sol or GPT-5.6 Terra. GPT-5.6 Luna currently has WebMCP disabled.
Site tools are not available in Enterprise or Edu workspaces. Availability also depends on rollout and the tools provided by the current page; updating alone does not guarantee access.
native_browser_setup.chatgpt_permission: In Settings > Browser > Permissions, ensure Enable site tools is on. Normal website-access/confirmation policies and per-invocation safety reviews still apply; they do not make site definitions or results trustworthy.
native_browser_setup.chatgpt_discovery: Open the direct live workbench in the top-level page. Select Site tools in the address bar, then Available site tools to inspect all six Offcut tools. Where available, Recently used opens Sources for recent calls. Regular browser/UI fallback actions are not WebMCP calls.
native_browser_setup.chatgpt_page_scope: The host currently supports top-level JavaScript-registered tools, not declarative form tools or tools in any iframe, including same-origin frames. Offcut uses the top-level imperative path. The built-in browser has a separate profile from normal Chrome: establish measurements in this host and keep the same document open through review/export. Closing or navigating away makes that page session's tools/plans/approval unavailable.
native_browser_setup.missing_site_tools: Check the app version, selected model, workspace, rollout, Enable site tools and direct top-level page against the official guide. Offcut registration-ready is not proof of host availability or model connection. These documentation prerequisites do not claim a visually verified ChatGPT desktop run.
native_browser_setup.native_version_boundary: Actual 1.1.0 checks used Chrome 149.0.7827.155 and 152.0.7977.64. Their clients discover a fresh real RegisteredTool with window/origin and JSON-string inputSchema, then executeTool(tool, JSON.stringify(input)); Offcut's object callback result is returned as a JSON string. Producer registration schemas remain objects. Pinned source declares registerTool undefined in 149 and Promise<undefined> in 152; the local void | Promise<void> type and await handle both. Observed callbacks received input only, so execute options are optional. Do not substitute an imitation record or a different draft's object-input client profile.

testing_instructions.agent_prompt: Inspect my Offcut workshop. Compare complete plans for all three objectives: least_stock, fewest_boards and least_waste. Respect protected stock and the current kerf/reusable-remnant settings. Account separately for sawdust, short scrap and reusable remnants. Stage the least-stock plan for my review. Do not approve it.

native_tool_workflow.expected_observation: Read the committed workspace, its current revision, protected stock, requirements, settings and pendingMeasurements. Confirm A-01 is protected. Use the returned revision, not an assumed number; finish/cancel pending edits before requesting review.

native_tool_workflow.inputs: Call once for each objective: least_stock, fewest_boards and least_waste. Supply expectedRevision from get_workshop and the objective. Omit excludedStockIds or supply an empty array for this scenario.
native_tool_workflow.expected_observation: Three new unapproved proposal records with actual returned IDs, complete/current and consistent with the sample. excludedStockIds are canonical additional exclusions, never an unlock of human protection. Repeating a valid same-revision/objective/additional-set request may reuse a retained checked solution; reusedFromPlanId discloses the actual source record, while a new computation reports null. Reuse never transfers approval.

native_tool_workflow.inputs: Supply planId using an actual ID returned by plan_cuts; inspect the alternatives.
native_tool_workflow.expected_observation: Exact layouts, part instances, offsets, material balance, freshness, exact approval, pendingMeasurements, canRequestReview and reusedFromPlanId. Check 14 produced parts, 7,000 mm finished length and no use of A-01. canRequestReview requires fresh && complete && !pendingMeasurements. Read the actual search proof status; on reuse, search.nodes and optimality describe the original search, not newly executed work or a new proof.

native_tool_workflow.inputs: Supply planIds containing the three distinct current complete proposal IDs, with least_stock first as the baseline.
native_tool_workflow.expected_observation: Actual metric deltas plus top-level protectedStockIds/sameConstraints and each row's canonical additional excludedStockIds/sameConstraintsAsFirst. Indicators compare the effective union of protected and additional IDs, without duplicate effective IDs. The sample has the same constraints: least_waste opens 2,880 mm more stock, handles three more pieces and has 158 mm less sawdust-plus-short-scrap waste, with sawdust unchanged. What-if different-constraint plans are allowed, but differences then cannot be attributed to objective alone.

native_tool_workflow.inputs: Before UI approval, supply the least-stock planId.
native_tool_workflow.expected_observation: The call is rejected with APPROVAL_REQUIRED. Generating, inspecting or comparing a proposal does not approve it.

native_tool_workflow.inputs: Supply the least-stock planId and current expectedRevision after all edits are finished/cancelled. Read get_workshop again; if a committed value actually changed, replan at the new revision before staging. A normalized no-op or cancelled edit does not itself change revision.
native_tool_workflow.expected_observation: With a fresh complete exact plan and no pending edits, review opens and the tool returns awaiting_human_approval, not approval. An otherwise valid request while pendingMeasurements is true instead returns ok:false with error.code PENDING_MEASUREMENTS before review publication, without blurring/saving the focused editor or opening a modal. It does not check acknowledgement or approve. Existing revision/ID/freshness guards still apply.

native_tool_workflow.inputs: Check the staged proposal against the illustrative inputs, tick the review acknowledgement checkbox, then click Approve cut sheet. Reject proposal is available instead.
native_tool_workflow.expected_observation: UI approval releases this exact ID for the current committed revision and page session. No registered tool approves. Rejecting a re-review of the currently approved ID revokes its approval; rejecting a different draft preserves the other exact approval. Keep UI-control approval outside the agent's permissions/workflow if the final decision is to remain with the person.

native_tool_workflow.inputs: After that UI approval, supply the same approved planId.
native_tool_workflow.expected_observation: CSV text with 17 columns (Part ID at index 8) and the full-plan-ID filename for the exact approved fresh complete committed plan. Native export remains intentionally allowed for that saved decision while editor drafts exist; it neither commits drafts nor grants approval. Human Download approved CSV and Print approved cut sheet remain paused until all edits are finished/cancelled. A committed value change makes the old release stale for both paths.

pending_measurement_checks: With committed kerf 3 mm, merely focus unchanged 3: pendingMeasurements stays false and a valid review may open. Type textual 03 instead: it is a draft and review is held until Enter/blur saves it or Escape cancels it. Saving the same numeric value normalizes text without changing revision; the still-fresh plan can then be staged.

With committed kerf 3 mm and a fresh sample plan, focus the kerf editor and type 4 without saving. Read pendingMeasurements:true and request review: expect PENDING_MEASUREMENTS, no modal, no blur/save, unchanged committed revision and the focused visible 4 preserved. Commit 4 yourself, read the new revision and observe old-plan staleness; replan before review. The actual revised14-part sample has56mm sawdust; its exact fresh plan is inspected and staged without new approval in the demonstration.

Invalid text such as 4.5 mm or an unfinished new row also keeps the shared flag true. Finish/cancel every draft. With two unfinished fields, cancelling only one must leave the other hold in place and must not erase an otherwise valid saved committed approval.

After approving an exact fresh plan, start an unfinished editor draft. Human CSV/print/review/approval pause, but approval is not lost per keystroke. Native export_cut_list of that exact committed approved ID remains allowed. Cancel all drafts to resume human release unchanged, or commit a real value change to invalidate the old approval and replan.
review_and_constraint_checks: Before approving, open Clear measurements without confirming it. Have the native host stage a fresh complete unapproved proposal; review interrupts the confirmation. Escape closes/rejects review, then Escape dismisses the resumed confirmation. Focus should return to the original Clear measurements control and the workspace must not be cleared. The single-confirmation Escape path also returns to its original control. This interleaving is covered by the current browser contract tests.

Stage the three-board least-stock plan, acknowledge it without approving, then have the native host stage the distinct six-board least-waste plan into the still-open dialog. The new exact ID must be announced, the heading focused and acknowledgement reset; inspect the six-board cut table before any separate approval. Re-staging the same ID is a strict no-op for focus/acknowledgement.

Re-review the currently approved ID and choose Reject proposal (or close review without approval, including Escape): its prior approval is revoked. Rejecting a different staged draft instead preserves the other exact fresh approved ID. Selecting another draft never substitutes that draft for the approved CSV/print source.

Open Full comparison references & restrictions with keyboard or touch. Zero additional exclusions does not mean zero protected stock. An additional set containing only an already-protected A-01 has the same effective constraints as an empty additional set; excluding another available board changes them. Fresh complete comparisons disclose that distinction. Do not combine today's protection with stale historical plan bases.
testing_instructions.reused_solution_check: Repeat a valid retained current-revision plan request with the same objective and canonical additional-exclusion set (input order may differ). Expect a new unapproved full record ID and reusedFromPlanId pointing to an actual retained record; the checked solution, original search.nodes and proof status are reused, not an approval or a new search proof. A genuinely new computation has reusedFromPlanId:null. Equal effective constraints from protected overlap do not make different additional sets the same reuse key. There is no cross-revision reuse. Controlled warm-solve and aggregate browser workloads are measured separately in the verification report, not claimed as model/judge latency savings.
revision_and_reload_checks: After release, change A-02's usable length from 2,400 mm to 2,399 mm and commit with Enter or blur. The workspace revision changes, retained proposals become stale and approval is invalidated; UI download/print are locked until a fresh complete plan is reviewed and approved.

On the native path, export_cut_list with the old approved planId now returns STALE_PLAN. A plan_cuts request using the old expectedRevision returns REVISION_CONFLICT. Read get_workshop again before a new request.

Reload the workbench. Validated measurements and protection can persist in localStorage when available; plans, approval, activity and tool-registration state are not restored as past decisions. Ephemeral pendingMeasurements resets false. Native registration runs again for the new document.
testing_instructions.source_instructions: The canonical linked guide contains complete source installation, production-preview, output-contract and observable-check instructions. No application secrets are required. Current source/native/browser/model/media execution records are repository-relative under submission/evidence and linked in the verification reports; source footage and the final MP4 are separate release assets.

physical_assumptions_and_limits.stock_model: One-dimensional crosscuts on a homogeneous batch of identical material and cross-section. Enter each physical board or existing offcut separately, using usable length after deducting end trim and unusable defects.
physical_assumptions_and_limits.per_stock_balance: sum(finished part lengths) + produced part count × kerf + final remnant = usable stock length
physical_assumptions_and_limits.kerf_convention: One saw pass per produced part, including the last; no free final factory-end cut is assumed. With 3 mm kerf, a 997 mm part fits a 1,000 mm usable length but a 1,000 mm part does not under this model.
physical_assumptions_and_limits.remnant_policy: A positive final remnant at or above the user-set threshold is reusable; a shorter positive remnant is short scrap; zero is neither. Waste is sawdust plus short scrap. Unopened stock and reusable remnants are not waste.
physical_assumptions_and_limits.confidence: Optimality is reported only for a complete result after valid exhaustive search/pruning. A complete result at the search limit remains feasible with optimality unproved. Failure to find a complete solution within a bound is not proof of infeasibility. Partial proposals identify missing quantities and cannot be approved or exported.
physical_assumptions_and_limits.release_boundary: Only the registered-tool capability boundary excludes approval, stock unlocking and inventory edits. It is not authentication of a physical human and does not prevent trusted same-origin scripts, developer tools or an agent with separately granted UI-control permissions from operating the page.
physical_assumptions_and_limits.inventory_limit: Approval/export do not reserve, consume or physically cut stock, and do not create a verified fabrication event. Record actual remaining usable inventory yourself for the next job.
physical_assumptions_and_limits.safety: This is a planning estimate, not machine-control instructions, a certified design or a safe-cutting guarantee. Verify stock identity, usable lengths, actual kerf, quantities and safe workholding at the bench.
physical_assumptions_and_limits.data_handling: Validated measurements are saved in this site's localStorage when available. Plans, approval and activity are page-session-only; pendingMeasurements is ephemeral, not a saved measurement or revision change, and resets on reload. The website has no application backend or model calls. A browser agent receives tool results and may process them under its provider's policies; hosting/browser policies also apply. readOnlyHint and untrustedContentHint are advisory, not trust/authentication/sanitization guarantees; read/export tools may append session activity.

verification_evidence.reporting_boundary: Current1.1.0 actual source/native/manual/browser/model/media evidence; prepublication working-tree build and pinned published JS delivery are distinguished in the report. eligibility.requirement: Confirm eligibility under Rules section 3 for the actual entrant and every team member, including legal age of majority, supported residence and geographic exclusions, promotion/judge relationships and conflicts. Review the rules' financial or preferential support restriction. GitHub login, repository ownership or a username establishes none of these facts.

entrant_and_representation.requirement: Choose individual, team or organization entry. Supply actual teammates rather than assuming a solo entrant. A team/organization must authorize an eligible representative to act and submit on its behalf; confirm each member's permitted team/organization participation.

ownership_and_submission_period.requirement: Confirm rights to the entrant's original contributions and compliance with third-party tool, source and asset licenses. Confirm creation during the submission period or meaningful WebMCP extension after its start. If pre-existing work applies, distinguish prior work from new work with the dated evidence required by the rules. MIT detection is verified; legal ownership and these entrant attestations are not.

Preparing this artifact does not register anyone, accept terms or authorize representation.
